name: Plant-fibre fabrics and cordage among early Andean foragers
summary: Foragers in the Peruvian Andes made plant-fibre fabrics and rope about 12,000 years ago, the oldest textiles yet found in South America.
description: Fragments of woven fabric and rope from Guitarrero Cave, high in the Peruvian Andes, were dated directly by accelerator mass spectrometry. The fabrics may have served as bags, baskets, wall or floor coverings or bedding, and bundles of processed plant material show that the work was done at the cave. The press release does not name the technique, so twining is not established here.

impact.note: Lowered from the lead's 2/2/2 because the origin is unknown and no descent from this community is shown: the finds witness fabric and rope making among early Andean foragers (reach 1), a basic capability for carrying, storing and bedding (depth 2), with later Andean fibre work as likely but unproven successors (generativity 1).

date.label: c. 10,150 to 9130 BCE (12,100 to 11,080 years ago)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Textiles from Guitarrero Cave were dated by accelerator mass spectrometry to between 12,100 and 11,080 years old, about 10,150 to 9130 BCE.

evidence.supports: to place the textiles at between 12,100 and 11,080 years old.
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'His team used the latest radiocarbon dating technique'

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.
